mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates expanding consumer demand and economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the Rank Information Coefficient (IC) between HOUST growth and S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which should lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns fail to correlate positively with PAYEMS growth in more than 60% of observations, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stronger supply chains and economic activity, which should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the Rank Information Coefficient (IC) between INDPRO growth and S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.2 percentage points while the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) does not adjust downward, it signals monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases > 0.2pp and FEDFUNDS does not decrease
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns do not show a negative correlation with this combined signal in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If retail sales (RSAFS) grow while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) declines, it indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 fails to show positive returns in more than 40% of cases when this combined signal occurs, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases while payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth slows, it signals monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative returns in more than 50% of cases when this combined signal occurs, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the Rank Information Coefficient (IC) between GDPC1 growth and S&P 500 returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, this hypothesis is rejected.
